# Psalm 45 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For-the-choirmaster. Upon Shoshannim [Lilies]. Of-the-sons of-Korah. A-Maskil. A-song of-love.

**2** My-heart overflows [with] a-good word; I-speak my-work to-the-king; my-tongue [is] the-pen of-a-skilled scribe.

**3** You-are-fairer than-the-sons of-man; grace is-poured on-your-lips; therefore God has-blessed-you forever.

**4** Gird your-sword on-[your]-thigh, O-mighty-one, [in] your-splendor and-your-majesty.

**5** And-in-your-majesty ride-prosperously, for-the-cause-of truth and-meekness-of righteousness; and-your-right-hand teaches-you awesome-things.

**6** Your-arrows [are] sharp — peoples fall under-you — in-the-heart of-the-enemies of-the-king.

**7** Your-throne, O-God, [is] forever and-ever; a-scepter of-uprightness [is] the-scepter of-your-kingdom.

**8** You-love righteousness and-hate wickedness; therefore God, your-God, has-anointed-you with-the-oil of-gladness above-your-companions.

**9** Myrrh and-aloes [and] cassia [are] all your-garments; from palaces-of ivory stringed-instruments gladden-you.

**10** Daughters of-kings [are] among-your-precious-ones; the-queen stands at-your-right-hand in-gold of-Ophir.

**11** Hear, O-daughter, and-see, and-incline your-ear; and-forget your-people and-your-father's house.

**12** And-let-the-king desire your-beauty, for he [is] your-lord; and-bow-down to-him.

**13** And-the-daughter of-Tyre — with-a-gift the-rich of-the-people seek-your-favor.

**14** All-glorious [is] the-daughter of-the-king within; of-gold-settings [is] her-clothing.

**15** In-embroidered-garments she-is-led to-the-king; virgins after-her, her-companions, are-brought to-you.

**16** They-are-led with-gladness and-rejoicing; they-enter the-palace of-the-king.

**17** In-place-of your-fathers shall-be your-sons; you-shall-make-them princes in-all the-earth.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **45:7**: 'Your throne, O God' — Hebrews 1:8 applies this directly to Christ. The king is addressed as 'God' (elohim) — the most exalted royal theology in the OT.

— EMET
